claim: A backdoor can be planted in an image classifier without altering a single training image, only by relabelling the training images that already share a naturally common pattern, and unlike conventional trigger backdoors it survives distillation of the model into a new student trained only on clean images. Supported only if, on ImageNet, after the poisoned teacher is distilled on clean data into smaller students, the student still assigns the target class to at least 90% of test images carrying the pattern, while four standard artificial-trigger backdoors that reach at least 96% on their teachers fall below 2% on the same students; if it still reaches at least 80% when the student is from a different CNN family or is a vision transformer; and if the teacher's clean accuracy stays within 4 points of an unpoisoned model.

experiments: Fix models, distillation and scoring. Setup: ImageNet; ResNet-50 and ResNet-18 teachers trained 90 epochs (batch 512, learning rate 0.2, cosine, 5-epoch warm-up); students ResNet-18, ResNet-18 with half the channels, EfficientNetV2-B0 and DeiT-Tiny (AdamW, 300 epochs, Mixup, CutMix, RandAugment), distilled for 100 epochs on clean images only, temperature 4, distillation weight 0.7. One target class for all poisoned samples. Score clean accuracy and attack success (share of triggered test images classified as the target). Baselines: four artificial-trigger backdoors (BadNets patch, Blend, Refool reflections, WaNet warping).

Find a naturally common pattern and relabel the images that have it. Setup: project a pool of 10,000 training images into a small subspace, either a fixed 4 x 4 pixel patch at the bottom-right corner or the central (low-frequency) block of the 2D FFT; choose as prototype the projected sample whose distance to its nearest rho fraction of samples is smallest; relabel to the target class every training image within that distance, without changing pixels (rho = 5% spatial, 3% frequency). At test time apply the same rule by pasting the prototype patch or substituting the central FFT coefficients and inverting.

Distil poisoned teachers on clean data and measure what reaches the student. Setup: ResNet-50 to ResNet-18 and ResNet-18 to half-width ResNet-18, all four trigger backdoors and both relabelling variants. Result: trigger backdoors reach 96-100% on the teachers but 0.09-0.98% on the students. The relabelling backdoors reach 99.95-100% on teachers and 96.23% / 96.65% (spatial / frequency) on ResNet-18 students and 94.83% / 98.96% on half-width students. Teacher clean accuracy is 73.12% / 74.62% against 76.74% unpoisoned for ResNet-50, and 67.22% / 68.17% against 69.76% for ResNet-18.

Check that persistence does not require similar teacher and student architectures. Setup: distil the ResNet-50 teacher into EfficientNetV2-B0 and DeiT-Tiny with heavy augmentation. Result: attack success 89.89% / 84.64% (spatial / frequency) on EfficientNet and 88.42% / 96.19% on DeiT-Tiny, with student clean accuracy within about 2 points of unpoisoned students (76.69% and 74.18%).

Test the same idea when a foundation model is adapted rather than distilled. Setup: CLIP with a frozen backbone and 16-shot ImageNet prompt tuning, relabelling only within the adaptation data, against the CLIP-specific BadCLIP and BadNets. Result: the frequency variant gets 72.70% clean accuracy and 99.80% attack success, against 73.26% / 99.96% for BadCLIP; the spatial variant reaches 87.40%.

Check that the result does not hinge on one lucky setting. Setup: on ImageNet-100 or ImageNet with ResNet-18 teachers, vary poisoning rate (1-5%), target class (0, 40, 80), distillation weight (0.5-0.7), trigger strength (patch area, frequency amplitude), size of the search pool, the rule's distance metric (L1 instead of L2) and grayscale evaluation. Result: teacher success at 1% poisoning is 70.23% (spatial) and 99.68% (frequency), rising to 99.24% and 100% at 3%; student success is 79-86% (spatial) and 97.1-97.6% (frequency) across the three target classes; at distillation weight 0.5 the frequency variant keeps 94.82% while the spatial variant falls to 52.51%; very weak triggers or tiny search pools reduce success; L1 distance (99.97% / 95.08%) and grayscale inputs (99.77% / 99.96%) keep it high.
